questions.stem: What does the woman say about the food at the canteen?
questions.stemZh: 女士对食堂的食物有何评价?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: I don't, actually. I personally think they're perfectly appropriate. 女：其实我不同意。我个人觉得它们（价格）完全合理。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者的直接应答 + 转折否定。男士先抛出 the prices are absurd 并反问 Don't you agree，女士的应答 I don't, actually 是一句明确的否定回应，紧接 I personally think they're perfectly appropriate——『被问者的直接否定+亮明己见』正是答案句信号，女 士的真实态度全在这句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: perfectly appropriate ↔appropriately priced 同根词改写：appropriate→appropriately priced

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 It is absurdly expensive. 直接挪用了录音里的 absurd，但说 the prices are absurd 的是 男士、不是女士，女士恰恰否定了这一点。听到 absurd 就选 A，正中『听到原词就选』的 陷阱。 借用原文：the prices are absurd C) 原词陷阱 It brings shame on the university. 借用了录音里的 shame，但男士那句 Shame about the food. 是英式口语『可惜了这食物』的意思，并非『给学校丢脸』，且也不是女士对食 物的评价。听到 shame 就联想到『丢脸』属于偷换概念。 借用原文：Shame about the food. D) 答非所问 It caters to students and teachers. 挪用了录音 both for students and teachers，但那 是男士在说食堂作为聚会点适合师生，谈的是场所、不是『食物』，与题目问的食物评价不 沾边。 借用原文：both for students and teachers

questions.stem: How does the woman feel about the canteen's sweet things or fancy delicacies?
questions.stemZh: 女士对食堂的甜食或精致美食有何感受?
questions.answerText: They never really appeal to her.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies. 我从来都不怎么想吃甜食或者什么精致美味。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 含蓄否定 never...crave 表态度。女士说 I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies，crave（渴望）配 never 是一句明确的『提不起兴趣』表态，正是答案信号 ——态度题就听这种带 never/really 的情感动词。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies ↔They never really appeal to her. 主被动视角转换：我不想要它 它不吸引我

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 答非所问 They are never actually good value. 蹭了录音里关于价格的讨论（desserts are overpriced），但题目问的是女士对甜点的『感受/兴趣』，女士给出的态度是『不想 吃』，而非评价它们『不划算』。把态度偷换成性价比。 借用原文：desserts are overpriced C) 与原文相反 They are within students' budgets. 挪用了前文男士谈预算的 beyond most students' budgets，且与原文相反（男士说甜点超出预算），更何况它讲的是价格不是女士的态度， 双重错位。 借用原文：beyond most students' budgets D) 张冠李戴 They always come at a high speed. 借用了录音里关于上菜快的描述（They also come out really fast），但那是男士夸炒蛋出餐快，被安到了甜点和女士态度上，张冠李戴又答 非所问。 借用原文：They also come out really fast

questions.stem: What did the canteen undergo a few years ago?
questions.stemZh: 食堂几年前经历了什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago. 据说他们几年前做过一次大规模的翻新。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 时间状语 a few years ago 标记答案句。女士说 they did a massive renovation a few years ago，时间状语 a few years ago 与题干完全对上，是答案句的定位信号；其谓语 did a massive renovation 即所问事件。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: a massive renovation ↔A massive renovation. 原词对应，但需与近义项 expansion 切开

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 A complete refurnishing. 蹭了改造话题，但 refurnishing 是『重新配置家具』，与录音 a massive renovation（整体翻新）程度和性质都不同，是偷换概念。 借用原文：a massive renovation B) 未提及 A ruinous burning down. 是『毁灭性烧毁』，录音通篇在夸食堂漂亮、做过翻新，根本没 提任何火灾，纯属无中生有。 C) 偷换概念 A substantial expansion. 与答案 D 同样表『大规模』，借 massive/substantial 的近似制 造混淆，但 expansion 是『扩建、变大』，录音说的是 renovation（翻新），并非扩大面 积，差在动作名词上。 借用原文：a massive renovation 1 W: Hi, Tony, today we're talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work. We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic. That's not really justified though, is it? W: 嗨,Tony,今天我们要谈谈管理者如何更好地与工作中的年轻人相处。我们经常听到说如今的年轻人缺乏 职业道德。不过这其实并不合理,对吧? 2 M: Not really. In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation. M: 确实不合理。实际上,这个年龄段的年轻人和其他任何一代人一样多样化和多面化。 3 W: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do? W: 是的,但如果你在工作场所与年轻人合作时遇到困难,你能做些什么呢? 4 M: Well, it's essential to connect with them to learn about their values. It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life. M: 嗯,与他们建立联系以了解他们的价值观是非常重要的。同样非常重要的是要认识到年轻人希望平衡工 作生活和个人生活的方式。 5 W: So they generally don't want to defer happiness in return for career advancement? W: 所以他们通常不愿意为了职业晋升而推迟幸福? 6 M: Absolutely. They are not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives and this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard. M: 完全正确。他们不愿意为了工作生活而牺牲个人生活,这导致人们将其等同于不愿意努力工作。 7 W: Right. But that couldn't be further from the truth, could it? W: 对。但这与事实相去甚远,不是吗? Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 8 M: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours, but they expect to have their time off, like weekends and nights free from work. M: 年轻人会在规定的工作时间内极其努力地工作,但他们期望拥有自己的休息时间,比如周末和晚上不受工 作打扰。 9 W: So how should managers go about assessing young people's productivity? W: 那么管理者应该如何评估年轻人的生产力呢? 10 M: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company. Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform. M: 一般来说,年轻人认为他们的生产力不应该用工作时长来衡量,因为有人可以工作八小时却几乎没为公司 完成任何有意义的事情。相反,年轻人通过他们所完成工作的质量来衡量自己的生产力水平。 11 W: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine. Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it? W: 但我们经常听到年轻人想要感觉自己不只是大机器中的一部分。这样的观点很难被否定,对吧? 12 M: It's important to legitimize their work. Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large. They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own. M: 使他们的工作合理化是很重要的。年轻员工想要从事对自己、对公司或对整个世界都重要的项目。他 们必须感到有必要继续在一家价值观与自己相符的公司工作。 13 W: Thanks for your advice. W: 谢谢你的建议。

questions.stem: According to the woman, what view about today's young people is not really justified?
questions.stemZh: 根据这位女士的说法,关于当今年轻人的哪种看法其实并不合理?
questions.answerText: They have a poor work ethic.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic. That's not really justified though, is it? 我们常听说如今的年轻人职业道德差。不过这种说法其实站不住脚，对吧？

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 女方自问句 + that's not justified。答案句出自女方之口：先抛出常见说法 young people today have a poor work ethic，紧接 That's not really justified though 直接呼 应题干的 not justified。「常听说……不过站不住脚」这个先立后破的句式，就是答案落点 的信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: young people today have a poor work ethic ↔They have a poor work ethic. 几乎原句搬到选项

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 选项 They don't get along with managers. 盗用了对话主题里反复出现的 managers，但 女方在 P1 里判为「站不住脚」的说法是职业道德差，从没说年轻人和管理者合不来，属答 非所问。 借用原文：young people today have a poor work ethic C) 张冠李戴 选项 They are struggling in the workplace. 借了后文 if you are struggling to work with young people 里的 struggling，但那是说「管理者难以与年轻人共事」，并非女方 在第 1 段判为不成立的看法，张冠李戴。 借用原文：if you are struggling to work with young people D) 张冠李戴 选项 They aren't as varied as their predecessors. 与男方 young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation 正好相反：男方说「和 任何一代一样多样」，选项却说「不如前人多样」，极性被反转，且这话也不是女方所说。 借用原文：as varied and multifaceted as any other generation

questions.stem: What does the man say is important for managers to get along better with young workers?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士认为管理者要与年轻员工更好地相处,什么是重要的?
questions.answerText: Recognizing how they try to strike a work-life balance.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Well, it's essential to connect with them to learn about their values. It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life. 嗯，与他们建立联系、了解他们的价值观是必不可少的。同样很重要的是，认识到年轻人想 要平衡工作与个人生活的方式。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 两个强调句 essential / important。男方连用 it's essential to 和 It's also really important to recognize 两处强调，正面回答「什么重要」。题干落在 work-life balance 一支，对应的正是 recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life 这句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life ↔ Recognizing how they try to strike a work-life balance. balance their work...life=work-life balance

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 选项 Learning about the way they adhere to their own values. 盗用了 learn about their values 里的 values，可男方说的是「了解他们的价值观」，不是「了解他们如何坚守 自己的价值观（adhere to）」，多塞了 adhere 这层原文没有的意思，答非所问。 借用原文：connect with them to learn about their values C) 原词陷阱 选项 Knowing how they struggle to connect with managers. 把 connect with them 的 connect 与别处的 struggle、主题词 managers 拼到一起，但男方说的是「与他们建立联 系去了解价值观」，从没说年轻人「难以与管理者建立联系」，纯属拼凑。 借用原文：it's essential to connect with them D) 原词陷阱 选项 Understanding the way they seek career advancement. 借了 defer happiness in return for career advancement 的 career advancement，但那出自女方提问、且说的是 年轻人「不愿」为升迁牺牲幸福；男方此处答「重要的是」并未把「理解他们如何追求升 迁」列为关键，张冠李戴又答非所问。 借用原文：defer happiness in return for career advancement

questions.stem: How do young people measure their productivity levels according to the man?
questions.stemZh: 根据这位男士的说法,年轻人如何衡量他们的生产力水平?
questions.answerText: By the quality of the work they do.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company. Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform. 一般来说，年轻人认为生产力不应以工作的小时数来衡量，因为有人可能干了八小时却几乎 没为公司做出任何有意义的成果。相反，年轻人是以他们所做工作的质量来衡量生产力的。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: not…by hours, Instead…by quality。男方先用 should not be measured by the number of hours 否定按时长，再用 Instead 引出真正口径 by the quality of the work they perform。Instead 之后才是答案落点，前半是被否定的干扰。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: by the quality of the work they perform ↔By the quality of the work they do. perform=do，其余原样

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 选项 In terms of the number of hours spent. 几乎照搬 the number of hours they work，但这恰恰是男方用 should not be measured 明确否定掉的口径，选它正中陷阱。 借用原文：should not be measured by the number of hours they work B) 偷换概念 选项 By the amount of work they perform. 借了原文的 work、perform，但把口径换成 「工作的数量（amount）」，男方说的是质量而非数量，偷换了概念。 借用原文：the quality of the work they perform C) 原词陷阱 选项 In terms of the work done in 8 hours. 盗用 work for eight hours 的 eight hours，但那只是男方举例说明「干八小时也可能毫无成果」、用来反证不该按时长，并非 衡量口径本身，答非所问。 借用原文：someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing

questions.stem: What companies does the man think would appeal to young workers?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士认为什么样的公司会吸引年轻员工?
questions.answerText: Those whose values align with their own.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large. They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own. 年轻员工想做对自己、对公司或对整个世界都有意义的项目。他们必然会想留在一家价值观 与自己一致的公司。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 末段总结句 a company whose values align。对话收尾男方给出结论 stay working at a company whose values align with their own，直接定义了吸引年轻人的公司类型。这是 对话末尾的总结落点，正面回答题干。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: a company whose values align with their own ↔Those whose values align with their own. a company=Those，定语原样

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 选项 Those whose culture facilitates their advancement. 把主题氛围词 culture 与女方 提问里的 career advancement 拼合，但男方末段说的是「价值观一致」，从没说公司文化 要「助推升迁」，纯属拼凑且不是结论。 借用原文：defer happiness in return for career advancement B) 偷换概念 选项 Those allowing them to do projects of their choice. 盗用 work on projects that matter 的 projects，可男方说的是做「有意义的（matter）」项目，不是「他们自选的 （of their choice）」项目，偷偷改了限定，与原文不符。 借用原文：work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large D) 原词陷阱 选项 Those refraining from discrediting their perspectives. 借了 Such a perspective can be hard to discredit 的 discredit、perspective，但那是女方提问里说「这种看法很 难被否定」，并非男方对「吸引人的公司」给出的特征，张冠李戴。 借用原文：Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it? Section B 1 Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes. Although it sounds counter-intuitive, restaurants Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests. 许多餐厅正试图说服顾客更可持续地饮食，从对环境不友好的肉类转向更环保的菜肴。一项新研究表明， 尽管听起来有违直觉，但在菜单上设置专门素食区的餐厅可能会无意中鼓励顾客吃肉。 2 Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study's authors, said, "Restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat. However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro-environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others." The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it. No vegetarians were included. They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends. Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters. But it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65%. The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation, or including a more appealing description of a non-meat meal, leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option. But our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror. The behaviors we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviorally fulfills all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out. The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present or when the marks were just placed on the mirror. Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. fish on the other side of a window. These results show either that fish are self-aware or that the mirror test, which is considered to be the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed. 这是一项证明动物自我识别能力的测试。只有少数动物，如人类、猿类、海豚和某些鸟类，能够在镜子中 识别自己。而且只有这些具备自我识别能力的动物，在镜子中注意到标记后，才会试图去除放置在其皮肤 上的标记。这种能力表明了更高水平的智力和意识。人类儿童直到大约18个月大时才表现出这种能力。到 目前为止，还没有鱼类展现出这种能力。但我们的实验表明，该鱼类在镜子中看到自己后，会在坚硬表面 上摩擦，以去除研究人员在其身上放置的标记。我们观察到的行为几乎毫无疑问地表明，这种鱼在行为上 完全符合最初制定的镜子测试的所有标准。在我们的研究中，当没有镜子存在时，或者当标记只是放在镜 子上时,该鱼从未试图去除标记。当未标记的鱼与窗户另一边的已标记鱼互动时，也不会试图去除自己身上 的标记。这些结果表明，要么鱼类具有自我意识，要么被认为是用于表示更高智力的黄金标准测试的镜子 测试可能存在缺陷。 3 What is less clear is whether these behaviors should be considered as evidence that fish are self- aware, even though in the past these same behaviors have been interpreted as self-awareness in so many other animals. Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviors in a fish satisfy passing the test at all. But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviors they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test? 不太清楚的是，这些行为是否应被视为鱼类具有自我意识的证据，尽管过去这些相同的行为在许多其他动 物身上被解释为自我意识。根据你的立场，你可能会拒绝接受鱼类的这些行为满足通过测试的解释。但 是，当它们表现出的行为与其他通过测试的物种在功能上如此相似时，你能在什么客观基础上这样做呢？ 4 Results from our research raise more questions than answers. What if self-awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer rather than appearing all at once? Perhaps in order to explore self- awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test. Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness, including where exactly fish fit in. 我们的研究结果引发的问题多于答案。如果自我意识像洋葱一样发展，一层层地累积而不是一次性出现， 会怎样？也许为了进一步探索自我意识，我们应该停止将对镜子的反应视为决定性测试。只有拥有更丰 富的自我理论和更大规模的测试组合，我们才能确定自我意识的各个不同层次，包括鱼类究竟处于什么 位置。

But does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print? As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens. But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and that parents talk less about content when sharing such books. 以往对幼儿的研究表明，包含额外功能（如词典和描绘故事情节的图像）的电子书可能比纸质书更有优 势。事实上，多项研究发现，电子书对故事理解和词汇量增长的支持超过了纸质书所能提供的。但也有研 究表明，儿童有时在从电子书学习时投入的心理努力较少，而且父母在分享这类书籍时对内容的讨论也 较少。 3 The study we're looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children. While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text. 我们今天关注的这项研究旨在让我们更好地了解电子书对幼儿有多好。在这项研究中，研究人员录制了17 至26个月大的儿童与其父母之一一起阅读的视频。每对亲子被随机分配阅读两本教育性电子书或两本内容 相同的纸质书。父母在朗读纸质书中的文字时，电子书则有配音演员朗读文本的音频。 4 The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books. A) Projects, relationships, and jobs don't always work out as planned — and it's not always clear when to give up. We've all repeatedly heard the saying that "quitters never win", but sometimes the best decision is to cut our losses.
B) Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable. Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever "it" is. And while perseverance is generally an excellent quality, it may also incline you to over-invest in something that is no longer a good idea.
C) As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don't want to "quit". But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't.
D) We are all susceptible to the sunk-cost delusion, an unconscious bias that leads us to persist in an endeavor we have already invested time, effort, or money into — even when abandoning it would be more beneficial. We realize that we can't get back the resources we've given, so we persevere — investing in a project that should be halted, staying in a relationship that should be over, or finishing a book we no longer enjoy and should put down, because we're already halfway through it. If quitting is "not your thing", you may be especially susceptible to this bias.
E) The sunk-cost delusion causes us to overly worry about what we'll lose if we move on and not think enough about the costs of not moving on. To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives. Ask yourself: What might I gain by cutting my losses now? Will you be happier or have time for another (better) opportunity? Then ask yourself: What will it cost me to soldier on? For example, is it possible that you'll be throwing more good money after what you've already lost? Or that you won't have the energy to capitalize on other promising possibilities?
F) The illusion of control can also interfere with our best judgment, leading us to overestimate our ability to control events and attain a positive outcome. This bias gives us a sense of agency and can promote mental health. However, the bias can also result in escalating commitment to a losing course of action. Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.
G) To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not. Think rigorously. While you may be able to influence other people and various circumstances, you can't force them to change or go your way.
H) Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere. With a written list in hand, you can ensure you focus on what you can control and better assess whether your continued efforts are worth the expense. Expending effort and emotion on things you can't control can be both draining and disempowering.
I) Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status.
J) Take my client Ryan, a leader at a technology company. Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear. As Ryan and I explored whether she should cancel the initiative she'd been leading or continue to persevere, she stated, "The thing is, I'm not a quitter." This singular, fixed sense of self was clouding her judgment and limiting her choices for action.
K) Our self-concept and identity are mental concepts that influence our behavior. If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept. To overcome this kind of internal obstacle, recall your other positive traits and personality characteristics. Ask yourself: What additional strengths do I have (or aspire to have) that would be helpful to employ here? For example, when I asked Ryan what other positive qualities from her personality she needed to leverage for decision making, she replied, "Discernment and bravery."
L) Now, examine your situation through the lens of each of these facets of yourself. What does the discerning part of you say? The brave part? Considering your decision through these different characteristics will enable you to see that you have more choices. It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit.
M) Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are. If you're considering whether to shut down your entrepreneurial venture, for instance, reach out to other founders as opposed to just your business partner. Similarly, if you're looking for love advice, ask someone removed from the ups and downs of your relationship instead of relying only on your best friend. In all cases, I recommend describing your situation and following up with a question like: "How would you manage this situation?" N) Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating. Sticking with the example of the entrepreneurial venture, numbers are your best friend. Use them to remove yourself from the love you have for this idea and consider your burn rate relative to growth plan, industry growth rates, and other factors that predict start-up success. External sources of information can help you see angles and possibilities you might not have considered. O) When something that seemed so promising at the start doesn't turn out the way we imagined, we can become overly self-critical. Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem. The most effective strategy here is to give yourself a break. Practicing self-compassion increases your resilience( 韧性), emotional intelligence, compassion toward others, and can boost your performance as well as help you develop a growth mindset. P) Instead of deliberating and criticizing yourself, focus instead on what you can learn from this situation. For example, Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project. And despite ultimately deciding to drop it, she was still happy she had tried and grateful for what the experience taught her. Q) Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed. But for your well-being, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action. While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities.

P1 People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.

P2 Under the guise( 外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.

P3 These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations. 

P4 When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.

P5 If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright(直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.

P6 The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?"

P7 If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self- regulate. As uncomfortable as it may be to continuously receive, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely defuse much faster.

P8 Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.

P9 It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress. 含 infer/imply/mainly。

reading-2.raw:
P1 As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.

P2 Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.

P3 What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "… a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."

P4 In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.

P5 One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism(社群主义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy are sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.

P6 Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.

P7 But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other — in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.

We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.

blocks.label: P2
blocks.text: Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.

blocks.label: P3
blocks.text: What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "… a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."

blocks.label: P4
blocks.text: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.

blocks.label: P5
blocks.text: One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism(社群主义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy are sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "It is believed that teachers can exert a profound influence on their students' academic pursuit and personal development." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
writing.model: It is believed that teachers can exert a profound influence on their students' academic pursuit and personal development. Having spent years in classrooms, I firmly agree that a dedicated teacher shapes not only what we learn but also who we become. On the one hand, teachers guide our academic growth. My high-school chemistry teacher, Mr. Li, turned a subject I once dreaded into my favourite one. By designing vivid experiments and patiently answering my endless questions, he inspired me to pursue science and eventually major in it at university. sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干一：中华民族 崇尚 自强自立精神（主语策略：原句主语） 这句中文其实是"一主多谓"：中华民族崇尚自强自立的精神 主语是"中华民族"、谓语"崇尚" (values/cherishes)、宾语"自强自立的精神"；后面 这一精神深植于中国文化之中，是民族生存与 发展的重要支撑 的主语换成了"这一精神"。处理上可拆成两句，或以"the spirit"为枢纽用定语从句 把后半句挂上去。主干立为 The Chinese nation values the spirit of self-reliance。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: "深植""是支撑"降级为定语从句 后两个分句 这一精神深植于中国文化之中，是民族生存与发展的重要支撑 都在补充说明"这一精 神"，可降级成一个 which 引导的定语从句挂在 self-reliance 后：…the spirit of self-reliance, which is deeply rooted in Chinese culture and serves as a vital support for the nation's survival and development。两个补充信息(深植、是支撑)用 and 在从句内并列，而不是把整句拆 成三段平铺。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时：values/is rooted/serves 都用现在时，因为这是对一种长期成立事实 的客观陈述。 语态 "深植于"是"被植入"的含义，英文用被动 is deeply rooted in，比直译主动更地道。 搭配 "是…的重要支撑"用 serve as a vital support for/provide vital support for；support 在此为不 可数，前面用 a vital support 或不加冠词皆可，别误用复数 supports。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Chinese nation values the spirit of self-reliance and self-improvement, which is deeply rooted in Chinese culture and serves as a vital support for the survival and development of the nation. 2. 改革开放以来，中国在自强自立的征程上，持续加大科研投入，在信息技术、人工智能、航 天工程等领域不断取得新突破。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 中国 加大投入 并 取得突破（主语策略：原句主语） 中国在自强自立的征程上，持续加大科研投入，在信息技术、人工智能、航天工程等领域不断取得 新突破 主语明确是"中国"China；有两个核心动作"加大投入"和"取得突破"，可作两个并列谓语： China has continued to increase…and has made…。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两状语前置 + 两动作并列 改革开放以来 译为时间状语 Since the reform and opening-up 前置；在自强自立的征程上 译为 on its journey toward self-reliance 作状语；在信息技术、人工智能、航天工程等领域 译为 in such fields as information technology, artificial intelligence and aerospace engineering， 作 made breakthroughs 的地点状语后置。两个动作用 and 连成并列谓语，避免拆成两个零散 短句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 本句偏离全篇基调：改革开放以来"持续""不断"表示从过去延续到现在的动作，用现在完成时 has continued to increase/has made，与 Since… 标志词搭配。 搭配 "加大科研投入"用 increase/step up investment in research (and development)；"取得新突 破"用 make new breakthroughs，breakthrough 可数、有"不断、新"之意故用复数 breakthroughs。 列举结构 "在…等领域"用 in such fields as A, B and C 或 in fields including…；最后两项之间用 and，别 全程逗号到底。

sentences.text: Since the reform and opening-up, China has continued to increase its investment in scientific research on its journey toward self-reliance, and has kept making new breakthroughs in such fields as information technology, artificial intelligence and aerospace engineering. 3. 5G 网络覆盖全国，远程医疗发展迅速，电子支付的使用全球领先，嫦娥探月工程展现了航天 领域引人注目的发展。

sentences.text: 四个并列分句各立主谓（主语策略：原句主语） 这句是四个各自独立的小分句：5G 网络覆盖全国/远程医疗发展迅速/电子支付的使用全球领先/嫦 娥探月工程展现了航天领域引人注目的发展，主语各不相同(5G 网络/远程医疗/电子支付/嫦娥工 程)。每个分句各立主谓，不能硬塞进一个主语。

sentences.text: 四短句重组：前三可并列、末句独立成句 前三个分句结构平行、信息密度相近，可用分号/and 串成并列：5G networks cover the whole country, telemedicine is developing rapidly, and the use of electronic payment leads the world；末句 嫦娥探月工程展现了航天领域引人注目的发展 信息较重，单独成句 The Chang'e lunar exploration program demonstrates remarkable progress in aerospace。避免四句一律 逗号平铺成 run-on。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时：cover/leads/demonstrates 都是对当下事实的陈述；"发展迅速"强 调正在持续，可用现在进行 is developing rapidly。 单复数与主谓一致 5G networks 用复数表泛指网络；the use of electronic payment 主语核心是 use(单数)，谓语用 leads；telemedicine 不可数，谓语用 is。逐句对一眼主语单复数再定谓语形式。 用词 "覆盖全国"cover the whole country/has nationwide coverage；"远程医疗"telemedicine；"电 子支付"electronic/digital payment；"引人注目的发展"remarkable/notable progress。

The Chang'e lunar exploration program demonstrates remarkable progress in China's aerospace field. 4. 自强自主精神成为推动国家现代化进程的强大动力，激励着中国人民为实现民族复兴 (rejuvenation) 的中国梦不断奋进。

sentences.text: 自强自主精神 成为 强大动力（主语策略：原句主语） 自强自主精神成为推动国家现代化进程的强大动力 主语"自强自主精神"(回指 glossary 统一译法 the spirit of self-reliance)、谓语"成为"has become/serves as、宾语"强大动力"a powerful driving force。主干立为 The spirit of self-reliance serves as a powerful driving force。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: "激励…奋进"降级为现在分词状语 后半句 激励着中国人民为实现民族复兴 (rejuvenation) 的中国梦不断奋进 是主语"精神"的又一动 作，降级为现在分词短语 inspiring the Chinese people to strive… 作伴随状语，挂在主句 后；"为实现…中国梦"译为目的状语 to realize the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation。避 免用 and 再起一个并列谓语显得松散。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时 serves as/inspiring，陈述当下持续的作用；若想强调"已经成为"也可 用现在完成 has become，与全篇协调即可。 非谓语逻辑主语 现在分词 inspiring 的逻辑主语须与主句主语一致——都是 the spirit，符合，故 inspiring 用得 稳；切勿让分词悬垂(主语错位)。 固定译名与搭配 "民族复兴的中国梦"按 glossary 译 the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation(原文已给 rejuvenation 提示)；"不断奋进"用 strive/forge ahead；"现代化进程"the process of national modernization/modernization drive。
